people.name: Mirjan Damaška
people.field: comparative criminal justice and international criminal law

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.object: Faculty of Law at the University of Zagreb
relations.evidence: he entered the Faculty of Law at the University of Zagreb in 1950... He graduated at the Faculty of Law in Zagreb in 1955.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: in his fourth year he gained a scholarship at the Hague Academy of International Law in the Netherlands.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: Next year, he gained a master's degree in comparative criminal justice at the International Faculty of Comparative Law in Luxembourg.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.object: Faculty of Law at the University of Ljubljana
relations.evidence: He gained his PhD at the Faculty of Law at the University of Ljubljana after successfully defending his dissertation, the Defendant's Testimony as Evidence in a Modern Criminal Proceedings in 1960.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: Between 1956 and 1957 he worked as a law clerk in trial and appellate courts. After that he choose a university career. He was named an assistant at the Faculty of Law in Zagreb in criminal proceedings.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: The next year, he became a bicentennial fellow at the University of Pennsylvania, where he taught until 1962.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: Two years after, he was professor at the International Faculty of Comparative Law in Luxembourg, where he remained for a year.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: In 1966 he was a visiting professor at the University of Pennsylvania until 1968.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: Damaška become the youngest full professor at the University of Zagreb in 1968, where he taught criminal proceedings in a department held by Vladimir Bayer.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: In 1970 he was named acting dean of the Faculty of Law in Zagreb.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: he went to the United States, where he taught at the University of Pennsylvania Law School from 1972 until 1976.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: Between 1975 and 1976 he was also a visiting professor at the Yale Law School.

relations.subject: Mirjan Damaška
relations.evidence: He took offer from the Yale University, and become a Ford Professor at the Yale Law School, where he teaches today as a Sterling Professor emeritus.

relations.subject: Vladimir Bayer
relations.evidence: Damaška become the youngest full professor at the University of Zagreb in 1968, where he taught criminal proceedings in a department held by Vladimir Bayer.
